newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to privatise one state bank this year.
newsitem.headline: Romania to privatise one state bank this year.

text.p: Romania's main privatisation agency said on Friday a long-awaited bank sell-off process would start this year with one of the country's six state-run banks going into private hands.

"We will privatise Banca Romana pentru Dezvoltare (BRD) before the end of the year," Sorin Dimitriu, president of the State Ownership Fund (FPS) told a news conference. "Also this year, we will start preparing the sell-off of Banc Post."
Dimitriu, speaking at the end of a meeting of the Romanian banking association, said privatisation of the two banks had won approval from the FPS board.
The FPS holds a controlling stake in most Romanian companies. It has a majority stake in state banks.
"Another bank that might be slated for sell-off is Banca Agricola, but it did not get a board approval," Dimitriu said.

He said share packages to be put on sale would be agreed upon at a later date. But sales would be targeted at strategic foreign investors, he added. "For banks, we need banking investors recognised in the international banking community."
Privatisation of state banks, a target agreed with international lenders, was given the green light earlier this year when a bank sell-off bill cleared parliament.
The law says privatisation of banks will proceed by a combination of raising bank capital through private or public share issues and sales of stocks held by the FPS.
The banking sector, one of the fastest growing in post-communist Romania, is made up of 42 commercial banks. No bank has been declared bankrupt so far.
Dimitriu said Western and local banks had shown interest in buying stakes in Romanian banks, but did not cite names. Under the law, local banks can buy up to 20 percent in any company.
Attempts to privatise state banks were made before, but they were unsuccessful as the leftist government, voted out of office last November, failed to introduce the necessary laws.

Development bank Banca Pentru Dezvoltare, farm lender Banca Agricola and Banc Post, which conducts savings operations through post offices across Romania, had been previously named as possible candidates for privatisation.

"Banca Agricola needs restructuring before privatisation and a programme to this effect will be submitted to government for approval by end-July," Dimitriu said, adding that the programme was expected to become operative in August.
